Its rules are mature and adversarial (template-lock, prompt-boundary preflight, proof-before-spend scouts, dimension-repair, separate geometry/style gates). The two biggest defects are: (1) the system never names a concrete image-GENERATION tool or command anywhere — generation is always an abstract "image model/tool," so the pipeline has no executable creative step; and (2) every cross-skill reference still points at `.codex/skills/...` even though skills now live canonically under `skills/`, resolving only via gitignored symlinks created by install.sh. lessons: Template-Lock Rule (skyline SKILL + workflow): the SVG owns production geometry; a generated image may propose artwork/silhouette but must never become the source of panel dimensions, seam/separator positions, saloon-arch width, red-zone positions, or guide strokes. Rationale: generated guide lines drift wider/shorter/lower and corrupt production geometry if trusted.

Prompt boundary preflight (skyline): before sending any prompt to image generation, strip template-geometry language; forbidden prompt concepts include SVG, contour, panel proportions, red zone, green line, orange arch, saloon-door guide, template guide, safe margin, production stroke. Rationale: inviting the model to 'honor/trace/fix' the template makes it redraw/reinterpret geometry; those constraints belong to deterministic overlay/export, not the creative prompt.

Artwork-only on white background (skyline + workflow): never ask the model to draw black borders, yellow margins, red zones, green contour, orange arch, door splits, or knobs; overlay the real SVG afterward and keep sky white so it can be removed/added later.

Geometry-Approved Style Adaptation Rule (style-agent + orchestration + AGENTS.md + drift_probes): when the user approves geometry/dimensions/location but rejects style, treat the approved raster as a composition/negative-space map ONLY and run an attachment-aware Whole-Panel Redraw; do NOT do locked-geometry local restyle, packet-crop collage, palette shift, or prompt-only substitute. Rationale: the 2026-06-16 top-temp lesson — rough B/C candidates were poor final art but excellent image-gen inputs; whole-panel redraw beat procedural placement polishing.

Style fit and geometry fit are SEPARATE gates; a metric PASS is a rejection gate only, never production approval (AGENTS.md, judge checklist, export_svg_template_fit emits 'MECHANICAL PASS ONLY'). A visual judge must inspect actual artwork/overlay/debug images. Rationale: mask metrics can pass while the image is clipped, scarred, or procedural.

Proof-before-spend scout gate (skyline): before a polished render, run 2-3 genuinely distinct low-cost scouts; faint lookalike placement boards are inventory maps, not approval evidence (differences must be visible within a few seconds). Rationale: prevents spending on a wireframe route that will fail.

Do not generate a rectangle and crop it; compose inside the contour first; final clipping is an exact-edge export guardrail only. Rationale: user explicitly rejected the 'cut down to fit' look (docs/workflow.md Screenery section).

SVG contours may be split across sibling elements; never diagonally auto-close an open path before checking sibling polyline/line segments (np01-back-bottom.svg lesson, encoded as the validator's space-socket regression). Sockets/notches are carved-out negative space even when their coords extend past the body bounds.

Landmark integrity / no-crop: buildings, landmarks, faces, birds, statues, signs, roof tips must read whole within their physical panel and must not be cropped by seams or red zones; run-through infrastructure (bridges, trains, rivers, rails) may cross panels only when it reads as continuous, not as a cropped focal subject (good vs bad fairy/castle example).

Flexibility rule: follow rules exactly where they protect production geometry or recognizable features; when strict interpretation is impossible/too slow/visually worse, follow intent, record the deviation, and ask the user if it changes the visual premise.
